Run Mode Selector

Quick Public One-Shot

10-20 minutes

Use at Mox/public tables when the adventure must fit into 2-3 hours.

Pregens required; one character question; one or two connections; quick rules primer; begin Prologue.

Guided Pregen Customization

25-45 minutes

Use when players want ownership without full build time.

Rename, pronouns, look, voice, motive, one equivalent Experience label, relationship to a faction. Do not change math/card loadouts unless Kyle permits.

Full Custom Character Session Zero

60-90+ minutes

Use only with a dedicated Session Zero or extended start.

Build/import Level 1 PCs, keep a Keystone Asset Custodian function, contract ties, connections, and a reason to continue after the job turns.

SZ-00 · Welcome / Table Frame

Establish tone, expectations, and the table's shared social contract.

Player Facing: Welcome to a beginner-friendly Daggerheart one-shot in Peril to Profit’s Goldspire Territories. We’ll learn by playing, build a party together, and start with a delivery job that becomes more complicated than advertised.

Purpose: Establish tone, expectations, and the table's shared social contract.

GM Notes
  • Keep it warm, confident, and short.
  • This is a paid public table: clarity and consent matter.
Session Zeroquick_pregen, guided_pregen, full_custom

SZ-01 · CATS / Campaign Calibration

Clarify concept, aim, tone, and subject matter.

Purpose: Clarify concept, aim, tone, and subject matter.

Concept: Corporate-fantasy delivery incident in the Goldspire Territories.

Aim: Learn Daggerheart, protect a community, and discover what the sealed delivery means.

Tone: 70% sincere fantasy, 20% corporate satire, 10% dark whimsy.

Subject Matter
  • animal danger
  • ambush
  • death
  • corporate exploitation
  • undead
  • memory/fear magic

                  S00-01 · The Job

                  Marlowe gathers trusted contractors to escort a sealed Keystone Asset to Hush.

                  A professional but slightly ominous delivery briefing. The crate is heavy, sealed, and important, but the full truth is withheld. The party starts inside the system rather than against it. Run this scene as contract / ordinary frame: The party begins inside the system: hired, trusted, and carrying more risk than they know. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

                  Marlowe Fairwind Emeris Crown Holdings Keystone Asset Goldspire Territories Ward Infrastructure Route Assurance Contract Sealed Keystone Crate Emeris Clerk Whitefire Custodian Escort Carriage Garrick Reed Varian Soto Slider System Hush
                  Scene State Controls

                  Player-Facing Read-Aloud

                  Marlowe checks the route map one last time. The sealed crate waits in the carriage, stamped with enough authorization marks to make opening it feel expensive.

                  Player Questions / RP Hooks
                  Questions
                  • What detail in The Job tells you the official story is incomplete?
                  • Who notices the human cost first, and how do they show it?
                  • What small object, smell, or sound makes this scene feel real?
                  Relationship Prompts
                  • Which PC quietly checks on someone else here?
                  • Who disagrees about the right thing to do without breaking trust?
                  Scene Ownership

                  Name one detail in The Job that belongs to your character's point of view.

                  Class / Ancestry / Community Reveals
                  • Loreborne or Knowledge-focused PCs can read the institutional layer.
                  • Wildborne/community-focused PCs can read local custom and ecological stress.
                  • Martial/security-focused PCs can read threat posture and custody logic.
                  • Magic-focused PCs can feel ward tone, soul-signal, or spell instability.
                  • Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding.
                  • Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits.
                  • Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk.
                  • Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness.
                  • Wildborne: reads the land, animals, and local ecological stress.
                  • Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage.
                  • Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.
                  Mechanics in Play / Official Result Roll Cards

                  Plot So Far: The party is in Prologue pressure: Marlowe gathers trusted contractors to escort a sealed Keystone Asset to Hush.

                  • Use Daggerheart Duality Dice as baseline.
                  • Apply the optional Slider System only if Kyle wants multi-band outcomes visible.
                  • Keep trivial actions no-roll; roll only when uncertainty, cost, or danger is interesting.

                  Trait Variety: Primary traits in this scene: Knowledge, Presence. If rolls drift toward Instinct/Presence, ask whether Agility, Strength, Finesse, or Knowledge better describes the action.

                  Read the contract pressureKnowledge, Presence · Hinge

                  Roll: Read the contract pressure

                  Trait Options: Knowledge, Presence

                  Why This Trait: Knowledge reads clauses; Presence reads what Marlowe is not saying.

                  Stakes: The job starts feeling routine when it is not.

                  Dice Mode: Roll Hope and Fear d12s, add the chosen trait, compare to the hinge, then read the higher die for Hope/Fear spin.

                  Dice Mode: Optional P2P Jenga Fear Variant, off by default and not official Daggerheart: roll one Hope d12 and use the tower for Fear only if Kyle enables it.

                  Official Daggerheart Results
                  Critical SuccessCritical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction.
                  Success with HopeSuccess with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous.
                  Success with FearSuccess with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure.
                  Failure with HopeFailure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option.
                  Failure with FearFailure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction.
                  Kyle Slider / House Adjudication Overlay

                  Kyle Slider / house adjudication style; overlay only, not official Daggerheart.

                  Botch <=D-5The job starts feeling routine when it is not. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
                  Miss D-4..D-1The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
                  Hit D..D+4The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
                  Clean D+5..D+9The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
                  Soar >=D+10The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: Goldspire Delivery Contract.
                  CritBest case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.
                  Hope Spin

                  Gain Hope. If using the Slider overlay, soften the band cost by one notch when it fits the fiction.

                  Fear Spin

                  GM gains Fear. If using the optional P2P Jenga variant, pull a tower block only when Kyle enabled that mode.

                  • Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
                  • Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.

                  The Logistics Incident

                  Threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test

                  Act One · The Logistics IncidentThreshold / transitionCorporate satire beatScene setup

                  S01-01 · Entering Sablewood™ Logistics Preserve

                  The carriage enters an ancient forest corridor rebranded as a safe logistics route.

                  The Old Sable is immense, living, and older than any corporate label. Goldspire has put its waymarkers into the ground, but the forest refuses to feel owned. Run this scene as threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test: The branded wilderness looks managed until the forest begins quietly disagreeing. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

                  Sablewood™ Logistics Preserve Goldspire Waymarkers Goldspire Territories Old Sable Varian Soto Barnacle Escort Carriage Khari Nix Hush Vendor Cart

                  Player-Facing Read-Aloud

                  The road narrows between colossal trees. Goldspire waymarkers glow at measured intervals, promising safe passage, customer delight, and limited liability.

                  S01-02 · The Overturned Vendor Cart

                  The party finds a vendor cart blocking the road, with spilled produce, invoices, and a useless incident placard.

                  This is the first crack in the official story. The route promised safety, but the cart is ruined, the driver is dead, and the system’s response is decorative. Run this scene as threshold into branded wilderness and first moral test: The overturned cart gives the party a mystery before it gives them a fight. Keep the camera close to practical choices, visible consequences, and the difference between ordinary people and the infrastructure pressing on them.

                  S01-03 · The Strixwolf Mother

                  A strange winged wolf-owl mother guards her pups while feeding from the dead driver.

                  Kyle Slider / House Adjudication Overlay

                  Kyle Slider / house adjudication style; overlay only, not official Daggerheart.

                  Botch <=D-5The wrong report protects the stack more than Hush. Use a hard complication, lost time, worse position, GM Fear, or mark Stress. Apply an official condition only if the fiction and rules justify it.
                  Miss D-4..D-1The attempt falls short, but a partial thread appears. Offer one clue, weak position, or safer follow-up.
                  Hit D..D+4The PC gets the core result, but it costs time, noise, leverage, or a visible resource.
                  Clean D+5..D+9The result lands cleanly. Give the useful truth or position without extra cost.
                  Soar >=D+10The result lands with leverage: add a bonus clue, better position, or future advantage. Possible loot: Lion-Sealed Writ.
                  CritBest case regardless of total: gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, and add a small concrete gift or clue.
                  Hope Spin

                  Gain Hope. If using the Slider overlay, soften the band cost by one notch when it fits the fiction.

                  Fear Spin

                  GM gains Fear. If using the optional P2P Jenga variant, pull a tower block only when Kyle enabled that mode.

                  GM Fear Spends
                  • Advance a visible timer or move a threat into better position.
                  • Reveal an omitted clause, route cost, ward symptom, or human consequence.
                  Relevant Official Conditions

                  None

                  Class / Community / Ancestry Reveals
                  • Every PC should name one truth they refuse to lose.
                  Official Conditions / Hazards
                  • No official condition unless a feature, hazard, or fictional position calls for Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable.
                  Search / Loot / Clues

                  No fixed loot. Offer clue, texture, or hospitality only when the fiction supports it.

                  No-Roll Guidance

                  Do not call for a roll when the players have time, a clear method, and no meaningful pressure.

                  Escalation / De-escalation

                  Escalate: Escalate by making cost visible: time, noise, trust, ward instability, or someone vulnerable in danger.

                  De-escalate: De-escalate through respect, care, honest testimony, useful evidence, or a concrete concession.

                  • Loreborne: spots older legal, heraldic, or ward-craft language under the branding.
                  • Underborne: notices service doors, hidden routes, and who built the thing nobody credits.
                  • Highborne: reads etiquette, class panic, and reputational risk.
                  • Ridgeborne: notices stonework, weight, pressure, and structural weakness.

                  • Elf/Ribbet/Human/Giant/Katari: invite one sensory or social detail from the player's heritage.
                  • Sorcerer/Rogue/Warrior/Guardian/Ranger: give each class one table-facing way to shine without changing the plot.
                  GM Details

                  End here. Do not over-explain the next adventure unless players ask.

                  Keep player-facing information actionable. Reveal systemic truth through objects, reactions, and consequences before naming it.

                  Searchable GM Rules Drawer

                  Daggerheart Table Support

                  #rules-canon

                  Action Roll Flow

                  Ask what the PC does, choose the trait that matches the fictional approach, set or reveal the Difficulty, then roll.

                  Roll Duality Dice, add the trait and any applicable Experience or bonus, compare the total to the Difficulty, then read Hope/Fear spin.

                  Roll only when the outcome is uncertain and the consequence matters. If there is no meaningful pressure, give the result without a roll.

                  #rules-canon

                  Duality Dice

                  Official default: roll two d12s, one Hope die and one Fear die.

                  Total the dice, add the relevant trait and bonuses, then compare to Difficulty.

                  The higher die determines whether the roll is with Hope or with Fear. Matching dice are a Critical Success.

                  Reaction rolls use the Duality Dice structure, but they do not generate Hope or Fear.

                  #rules-canon

                  Hope/Fear Outcomes

                  TotalSpinResult
                  >= DifficultyHopeSuccess with Hope: get what you want and gain Hope.
                  >= DifficultyFearSuccess with Fear: get what you want, but there is a cost or consequence; GM gains Fear.
                  < DifficultyHopeFailure with Hope: things do not go as planned, but gain Hope.
                  < DifficultyFearFailure with Fear: things go badly; major consequence or complication; GM gains Fear.

                  #rules-canon

                  Critical Success

                  When the Hope die and Fear die match, the roll is a Critical Success.

                  A Critical Success counts as a roll with Hope even if the total would otherwise miss the Difficulty.

                  On a Critical Success, the PC gains Hope and clears 1 Stress. On an attack roll, follow the official critical damage rules.

                  #rules-canon

                  Difficulty Ladder

                  DifficultyNumberUse
                  Very Easy 55Obvious, low-pressure, strong leverage, or beginner-friendly on-ramp.
                  Easy 1010Low pressure, beginner-friendly, obvious route.
                  Average 1515Default meaningful uncertainty.
                  Hard 2020Dangerous, contested, or specialized task.
                  Very Hard 2525Exceptional, unstable, rushed, or opposed.
                  Nearly Impossible 3030Legendary attempt; usually offer another route.

                  #rules-canon

                  Traits

                  TraitWhat it covers
                  AgilitySprint, leap, maneuver, dodge, balance, climb fast, keep footing.
                  StrengthLift, smash, grapple, hold, carry, resist force, endure strain.
                  FinesseControl, hide, tinker, pick, disable, handle delicate details.
                  InstinctPerceive, sense, navigate, track, read danger, read animals.
                  PresenceCharm, lead, soothe, deceive, perform, intimidate, negotiate.
                  KnowledgeRecall, analyze, investigate, comprehend, reason from lore.

                  #gm-aid not official

                  D&D-to-Daggerheart Translation

                  D&D Conversion

                  Daggerheart uses traits, not D&D skills. Pick the trait that matches the player's fictional approach.

                  Use the D&D conversion page as a GM aid for players arriving from 5e; it is not official Daggerheart rules text.

                  #rules-canon

                  Advantage / Disadvantage

                  Advantage adds a d6 advantage die to the roll total.

                  Disadvantage subtracts a d6 disadvantage die from the roll total.

                  Advantage and disadvantage cancel each other out before rolling. If multiple advantage dice remain, use the highest one.

                  The GM may grant advantage or disadvantage when the fiction supports it.

                  #rules-canon

                  Experiences, Help, Tag Team

                  Experiences are short backstory/expertise phrases. Spend 1 Hope before a roll to add a relevant Experience modifier.

                  Help an Ally: spend 1 Hope, describe feasible help, roll a d6 advantage die, and add it to the acting PC's roll using the normal advantage rules.

                  Tag Team Roll: once per session, spend 3 Hope to combine two PCs' efforts. Both roll, choose one result for both, and resolve as a single action roll.

                  #rules-canon

                  Hope Uses / Fear Uses

                  Hope can be spent to Help an Ally, use Experiences, initiate a Tag Team Roll, or activate Hope Features.

                  On a roll with Fear, the GM gains Fear and makes a move reflecting the complication.

                  Fear can be spent to spotlight adversaries, use Fear Features, make stronger GM moves, apply adversary Experiences, and advance pressure when the rules or stat block call for it.

                  #rules-canon

                  GM Moves / Adversary Spotlight

                  GM MovesAdversary Spotlight

                  The spotlight moves through the fiction rather than a fixed initiative order.

                  The GM commonly makes moves when a PC rolls with Fear or fails an action roll.

                  Use softer moves to telegraph, reveal, or reposition. Use harder moves when the fiction and result call for direct consequence.

                  Spend Fear or use features when the adversary/environment rules call for it.

                  #rules-canon

                  Adversary Attack Rolls

                  Adversary Attack Rolls

                  Adversaries roll a d20 plus their attack modifier against the target PC's Evasion.

                  PCs do not roll defense by default. Use reaction rolls only when a rule, feature, or GM call gives one.

                  PC action rolls against adversaries use the adversary's Difficulty from the stat block.

                  #rules-canon

                  Damage / Armor / Stress

                  Damage / Armor

                  Compare incoming damage to the character's damage thresholds to determine how many HP are marked.

                  Mark an Armor Slot to reduce the severity of incoming damage by one threshold.

                  When a character marks their last Stress, they become Vulnerable until they clear at least 1 Stress.

                  If a character must mark Stress while all Stress slots are marked, follow the official overflow consequence from the character rules.

                  #rules-canon

                  Short Rest

                  A short rest is about an hour to catch breath and recover.

                  Each PC may swap domain cards between loadout and vault, then choose two moves, including choosing the same move twice.

                  Short rest moves: Tend to Wounds, Clear Stress, Repair Armor, or Prepare.

                  Prepare gains Hope; preparing with one or more party members gives each of those PCs 2 Hope.

                  #rules-canon + module tracker

                  Countdown

                  Countdowns are visible pressure clocks. Tell players what changes when a countdown ticks.

                  On progress countdowns, successful action rolls can tick the party closer to the goal.

                  On consequence countdowns, failures or success with Fear can tick the opposing pressure closer.

                  Open Vale uses a module ritual countdown as a tracker; do not treat it as a new condition.

                  #rules-canon

                  Ranges

                  Use Daggerheart range bands at the table: Melee, Very Close, Close, Far, Very Far, and Out of Range.

                  When exact distance is not important, keep ranges conversational and tied to reachable action.

                  #rules-canon

                  Official Conditions

                  Official Conditions

                  Daggerheart has three primary global conditions: Hidden, Restrained, and Vulnerable.

                  Some features create unique effects, but those are feature-specific text, not module-wide conditions.

                  Unless a rule says otherwise, the same condition cannot stack on one target.

                  Temporary conditions can be cleared with a fitting action roll, a GM-approved fictional method, or by an adversary spending its spotlight to clear the condition.

                  Unconscious appears only as Death Move/status context in this Atlas, not as a global condition card.

                  #slider house table style

                  Kyle Slider / House Adjudication

                  Kyle's Slider is a house/table adjudication overlay for degree of outcome.

                  It sits on top of official Daggerheart results and never replaces Success with Hope, Success with Fear, Failure with Hope, or Failure with Fear.

                  Use it only to decide how much fiction, cost, or leverage to attach to the official result.

                  BandTotal vs DifficultyUse
                  Botch<= D - 5Failure and the situation worsens.
                  MissD - 4 to D - 1Failure with a partial thread or near miss.
                  HitD to D + 4Success at a cost.
                  CleanD + 5 to D + 9Clean success.
                  Soar>= D + 10Success plus extra leverage.
                  Critmatching diceTop outcome, gain Hope, clear 1 Stress, small gift.

                  #p2p optional off by default

                  P2P Jenga Fear Variant

                  Optional only and off by default. This is not official Daggerheart.

                  Default play uses official Duality Dice: two d12s, Hope and Fear.

                  If Kyle enables the variant, roll one Hope d12 and use the tower to resolve Fear pressure.
